messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@medflow.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MediFlow MAP: capacity triggers & lead-time asks

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the kickoff today. As promised I'm attaching an updated MAP template (MediFlow_MAP_v3.xlsx) that folds in the capacity and procurement milestones we discussed. Before we lock milestones into the MAP, can you confirm the following so we can size Dedicated vs Private GPU pools accurately: 

- Target go-live / first-production-traffic date (we discussed late Q3, but what is your target?)
- Expected steady-state QPS or requests/minute to the generation endpoint (ballpark is fine)
- Peak concurrency (how many simultaneous users/requests at peak) and acceptable 95th/99th latency SLOs
- Model variants you expect to serve (e.g., 7B chat, 70B instruction, quantized MPT-style) and whether you need non-quantized FP16 for a subset
- Any data residency / on-prem compliance constraints (we flagged Private if so)

Two lead-time items to call out that will affect the MAP timeline: 
1) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) procurement and provisioning typically takes 6–10 weeks after contract signature for standard cloud regions; H100 availability can push to the high end.
2) Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments add customer-side infra prep and KMS/HSM integration time — plan 10–14 weeks for a first on-prem rollout (networking, security review, acceptance testing).

If you can return the forecast sheet I attached (MediFlow_infra_forecast.xlsx) with the QPS/concurrency columns filled, Naomi and I will produce a short capacity estimate and tranche-based handoff plan for the MAP. Also attached: SOC2_evidence_requirements.pdf so you know what we’ll need for security gating.

Next step: Can we schedule a 30-min MAP milestone walk-through with your infra and procurement teams this week? 

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MediFlow_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2_evidence_requirements.pdf (doc)

Hi Priyom / Naomi —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers below; I attached our internal infra forecast as requested.

- Target go-live: 2027-09-15 (can be phased; pilot users first two weeks)
- Steady-state QPS: ~18 req/s for baseline workflows (we expect burstiness up to 80 req/s during reporting windows)
- Peak concurrency: assume up to 40 concurrent generation sessions; target p95 latency < 350ms
- Models: primary is a 70B instruction model (quantized acceptable for steady routes), a smaller 13B chat variant for low-latency flows; we will need an FP16 profile for the 70B when accuracy/regulatory flows are gated
- Data residency: US-only for now; Private deployment is optional but procurement prefers Dedicated unless we need on-prem for audits

Attachments: MediFlow_infra_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Procurement note: our legal/procurement timelines are usually 6–9 weeks after final SOW. If Private required, we’ll add an additional security review window (~4 weeks). Happy to do the walk-through — I’m available Wed 4/21 10–11am PT.

—Claire
Head of ML Ops, MediFlow

Thanks Claire — the numbers are very helpful. I pulled a quick tranche-sizing estimate based on the forecast you sent. High level notes: 

* Baseline pool (phase 1 pilot) — support 18 req/s steady with headroom for 2x bursts: 4 x A100-80GB or 2 x H100-80GB (quantized–friendly).
* Production pool (phase 2) — to hit 80 req/s bursts with p95 < 350ms and room for cache priming, recommend a 6 x H100-80GB reserve (or 10 x A100-80GB as a cost-hedge).
* FP16 runway — as you noted, regulatory flows should have FP16/FP32 profile; plan to reserve 2 H100s that are non-quantized-capable or schedule fallback policy for those routes.

Quick latency/concurrency calc (very rough):
- avg tokens per request: 150
- tokens/s capacity per H100 (w/ batching & KV cache): ~1200 tokens/s
- concurrent sessions estimate -> 40 * 150 tokens = 6000 tokens in process -> ~5 H100 equivalents at sustained peak (so 6 for headroom)

Operational recommendations for the MAP: 
1) Tranche approach: pilot (1–2 weeks) -> scale node count and enable prefix cache -> final acceptance.
2) Acceptance test: 72-hour stress run with production traffic replay (we’ll provide harness).
3) Fallback rules: model variant fallback (70B -> 13B) and region fallback if Dedicated capacity shortages occur.

I attached a short PDF with the calculation and a conservative timeline for Dedicated vs Private provisioning.

—Naomi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_estimate_20270418.pdf

Team —

Nice thread. I sketched a minimal MAP milestone set for procurement and ops handoffs; linking here: https://redwood.example.com/s/plan/MF-2027-042 (editable). Key procurement triggers I propose we put into the MAP: 

- M1: SOW signed -> allocate initial tranche (pilot pool allocation) within 7 business days
- M2: Pilot acceptance -> commit to production pool sizing (week window) -> issue reserved capacity order (6–10 week delivery depending on SKU)
- M3: Security acceptance (SOC2 gating) -> Private deployment kick if requested (adds 10–14 weeks)
- M4: Production cutover canary -> enable route-level throttles + monitoring for 2 weeks -> final acceptance

For MAP clarity, we should capture SLAs around provisioning (e.g., delivery calendar for H100 vs A100), and an explicit rollback window if procurement slips. Priyom — can you own the M1/M2 owner assignments? Naomi — please add the acceptance test checklist to the shared doc. Claire — can procurement and infra owners from MediFlow be added to the hub link?

—Ben
Director, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Ben / team —

This looks good. Quick confirmations from our side: 
- We accept the tranche approach and the M1–M4 milestones.
- Procurement cadence: we can sign SOW by 2027-05-06 assuming final T&Cs; that lines up procurement delivery for Dedicated H100 tranche by mid-August (~11–12 weeks).
- Private option: we'll keep Private in scope for audit-critical routes but will initially proceed with Dedicated for speed to market. If Dedicated availability becomes constrained, we’ll engage Private and expect the additional 4-week security review.

Next steps: Priyom — please add the finalized M1 dates to the HubSpot deal and send an updated MAP with the procurement calendar embedded. Naomi — we’ll accept your 72-hour stress-run as the acceptance test; please ship the harness and any test data requirements.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough on Wed.
